name: Gyeli
catalog_citation: Grimm, Nadine. 2021. A grammar of Gyeli (Comprehensive Grammar Library 2). Berlin: Language Science Press. Open-access PDF, zenodo.org/records/4737370.
catalog_locator: ch. 2 Phonology, §2.4 Tonology, pp. 97-98 (also §2.3.1 p. 80 on syllable as TBU)
catalog_quote: Gyeli is a tonal language. It uses pitch differences to make both lexical and grammatical distinctions. ... Tone attaches to segmental units which are called “tone bearing units” (TBUs). Whether the TBU is the segment (e.g. vowel or nasal consonant), mora, or syllable is language specific and may vary across even closely related languages. In Gyeli, the TBU is the syllable. As discussed in §2.3.1, Gyeli has heavy and light syllables, differing in the number of weight units which are called “moras”. Heavy syllables have two moras, light syllables only one. The reason why in Gyeli the syllable must be the TBU is that heavy and light syllables bear the same number of tones ... Gyeli possesses level tones, contour tones, and underlyingly toneless TBUs which surface phonetically as L or are assigned an H tone by their environment. ... Gyeli has two level tones: H and L, as contrasted in (66)…

audit.reasoning: The classification 'tonal, no word-stress rule described' rests on the best available source: a 701-page 2021 open-access reference grammar by the language's principal fieldworker, held on file, with the deciding quotation confirmed verbatim at the stated pages (97-98). A full-text grep of the grammar finds no stress/accent/prominence statement. The one additional phonological study found (Grimm 2022, Phonology, CC-BY, fetched sources to restates the same tonal system (H, L, HL, LH, toneless TBUs; syllable = TBU) and never mentions stress or accent, so it confirms the coding. Only cosmetic fix available: the parenthetical secondary locator 'section 2.3.1 p. 80' should read p. 87. No recode, no identity issue (Gyeli = Bagyeli/Bakola, Bantu A801, glottocode gyel1242 matches the Zenodo record held).

sources.citation: Grimm, Nadine. 2022. Exponence and the functional load of grammatical tone in Gyeli. Phonology 39(3): 473-501. doi:10.1017/S0952675723000131 (CC-BY 4.0; online Nov 2023).
sources.quote: p. 476: 'Phonologically, Gyeli distinguishes level tones (H and L), contour tones (HL and LH) and toneless (null) tone-bearing units (TBUs). Valued TBUs are lexically specified for H, L, HL or LH, whereas unvalued TBUs are underlyingly toneless.' p. 477: 'Rising and falling tones ... are true contour tones in Gyeli, as I analyse the syllable as the TBU (instead of the segment or mora).' The article describes eight grammatical tones in simple predicates; the words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur in the body text (grep of full extracted text).
